_comment: Asset-class registry for tools/asset-gen. This is the single extension point:
adding an asset class means adding an entry here plus a prompts/<promptFile>,
never a branch in gen.py. Mirrors the engine's own data-drives-the-code rule.
geometry.size is the FINAL on-disk pixel size the engine expects. geometry.cell
and geometry.frames describe grid sheets; the post-processing pipeline slices the
model's output into that grid. 'post' names steps in lib/postprocess.py, applied
_styleTagsComment: Tags for local Stable Diffusion 1.5, and deliberately NOT the retro pixel
Two reasons. CLIP reads 75 tokens per chunk and weights the earliest most,
so the prose bible buries the material being drawn, and it cannot negate --
the bible's NEVER list actively summons what it forbids. Prohibitions live
But the bigger reason is that ASKING for pixel art is the wrong request.
SD1.5 renders 'pixel art' as a blurry imitation of it. Ask instead for the
best, sharpest, most detailed version of the real material, and let the
pipeline do the conversion: rendering at 512 and reducing 4x to 128 with a
palette clamp IS the pixelation, and it produces true hard pixels rather
than a picture of some. Detail in the source becomes legible texture after
the squash; mush in the source becomes mush.
styleTags: masterpiece, best quality, highly detailed, sharp focus, 4k, detailed painted source
styleBible: Retro JRPG pixel art in the RPG Maker 2003 / late-90s SNES-to-PS1 tradition. Chunky legible pixels, hand-placed dithering rather than smooth gradients, a tight limited palette, strong silhouette readability at small size. Dark low-fantasy dungeon-crawler mood: grimy stone, muted earths and desaturated jewel tones, torch-warm highlights against cold shadow. NEVER: modern vector art, cel-shaded anime line art, watercolour, 3D renders, drop shadows, text, labels, watermarks, signatures, UI frames, or borders.

smallBattler.label: Small battler
smallBattler.note: Idle animation strip drawn in the party grid and status rows. presentation/small_battlers.lua reads the [fps=N] token from the FILENAME.

bigBattler.label: Big battler
bigBattler.note: NEW CLASS: the full-size enemy/creature battle sprite, split out from the double-duty 'spriteKey' portrait lookup. Generates and promotes today; the engine does not read assets/bigBattlers yet (see README 'Pending engine wiring').

portrait.label: Portrait (expression sheet)
portrait.negativePrompt: pixel art, pixelated, low resolution, jpeg artifacts, perspective, vanishing point, horizon, 3d render, photograph, photorealistic, scene, landscape, objects, furniture, drop shadow, cast shadow, vignette, lighting gradient, smooth gradient, blurry, depth of field, bokeh, border, frame, picture frame, grid lines, text, letters, watermark, signature, vector art, cel shaded, anime lineart, watercolour, multiple people, crowd, extra limbs, malformed face
portrait.note: presentation/ui.lua slices column 0 as the neutral face; the sheet is 5 x 128x192 columns. NPC files conventionally carry the NPC_ prefix.

sprite.label: World sprite (3D billboard)
sprite.note: Drawn as a whole billboard in the raycast viewport (presentation/viewport_3d.lua slices it by column, so it must NOT be a multi-frame sheet). Faces the camera; feet at the bottom edge.

tileset.label: Tileset texture page
tileset.note: 16 seamlessly-tiling 64x64 surface textures, row-major. Wall/floor/ceiling textures sampled by the raycaster: flat head-on, no perspective, no baked lighting.

texturePiece.label: Single tileset texture piece
texturePiece.note: Generate one coherent floor/ceiling/trim material at a time. Use wallPiece for walls, then assemble selected pieces into a 4x4 tileset atlas with assemble_atlas.py.

wallPiece.label: Single horizontally tileable wall texture piece

contextPreview.label: two-tile corridor; shared wall height map; 4.0x geometry density; floor and ceiling unchanged

wallPiece.note: Generate one wall material at a time. Only the left and right edges are joined; the top and bottom remain authored, so baseboards and lower wall courses stay at the bottom. Assemble selected pieces into a tileset atlas with assemble_atlas.py.

portraitPiece.label: Single character portrait piece
portraitPiece.negativePrompt: pixel art, pixelated, low resolution, jpeg artifacts, perspective, vanishing point, horizon, 3d render, photograph, photorealistic, scene, landscape, objects, furniture, drop shadow, cast shadow, vignette, lighting gradient, smooth gradient, blurry, depth of field, bokeh, border, frame, picture frame, grid lines, text, letters, watermark, signature, vector art, cel shaded, anime lineart, watercolour, multiple people, crowd, extra limbs, malformed face
portraitPiece.note: Generate one fixed-framing character portrait at a time. Assemble five selected expression pieces into the engine's 640x192 sheet with assemble_atlas.py.

surface.label: Image-authored geometry surface (albedo)
surface.note: The albedo half of an engine/geometry asset -- one seamless material, rendered at 512 and downsampled 4x. Registration is a hard rule: the albedo must match its sibling height.png pixel for pixel, so pass --cell WxH when re-skinning an asset whose height map is not 128x128.

panorama.label: Panorama / skybox
panorama.note: Scrolled horizontally behind the dungeon view, so it must wrap left-to-right; seam_blend_x cross-fades the wrap edge.

locationArt.label: Location art
locationArt.note: Establishing illustration for a town or dungeon region.

eventArt.label: Event art
eventArt.note: Wide cutscene banner shown above dialogue.

animation.label: Particle / animation sheet
animation.note: Flipbook strip, cells left-to-right, read row-major by the animation player. Tinted at runtime by the track's colour-over-lifetime, so the art is drawn WHITE/GREYSCALE. Final size is cell*frames wide; --cell and --frames override the defaults and are written into the filename tokens.
